draft.title: Independent and dependent variables
card: Bivariate data has two numerical variables. When they may be linked, we ask which one might explain or predict the other.
the variable that may explain or predict changes in the other. It goes on the horizontal axis.
the variable that may depend on the other. It goes on the vertical axis.

Example: a teacher studies hours of study and test score. Hours of study may explain the score, so hours is independent and score is dependent. Choosing the independent variable is a judgement about which could predict the other, and it does not prove that one causes the other.
draft.remember: Independent may explain or predict. Dependent is what may change. Independent goes across.

a.q: Mia records the daily hours of sunshine and the number of ice creams sold at her kiosk in Manly. She wants to predict sales from sunshine. Which is the dependent variable?
opts: Number of ice creams sold
Hours of sunshine
The day of the week
The price of an ice cream
a.why: Mia wants to predict sales from sunshine, so sales is the dependent variable. Hours of sunshine is the independent variable, the one used to explain or predict.

b.q: Sam measures the height and forearm length of 20 students. He wants to predict height from forearm length. Which statement about his scatter plot is correct?
opts: Forearm length goes on the horizontal axis
Height goes on the horizontal axis
Forearm length is the dependent variable
Either variable can go on the horizontal axis
b.why: Sam predicts height from forearm length, so forearm length is independent and goes on the horizontal axis. Height is dependent and goes on the vertical axis. The axis is chosen by which variable is used to predict, not by which is bigger.
b.clue: Which variable is being used to make the prediction?

b.best: Forearm length goes on the horizontal axis

problems.detail: 'Dependent is what may change' is loose: both variables change. The card says the dependent variable is the one that may depend on the other. A student could wrongly take it that the independent variable does not vary. Better: 'Dependent may depend on it.'

check.summary: Both questions are correct and their explanations agree with the card. The only issue is that the remember line calls the dependent variable 'what may change', which is looser than the card's 'may depend on the other'.
